root_cause.text: rxrpc_recvmsg() in the RXRPC recvmsg queue logic blindly re-added a call to rx->recvmsg_q on the MSG_DONTWAIT error path without checking whether call->recvmsg_link was already queued, causing list corruption and mismatched call references.
root_cause.evidence: The commit message states the call was "requeue[d] - whether or not the call is already queued" and that this "may then corrupt the recvmsg queue, leading to things like UAFs or refcount underruns"; the patch fixes this by testing `list_empty(&call->recvmsg_link)`, otherwise either leaving it at the front or `list_move()`-ing it, and by dropping the extra reference with `rxrpc_put_call()` when no new queue insertion occurs.

intent_record.intent_summary: Add the missing trace reason mapping for rxrpc_call_put_recvmsg_peek_nowait so runtime debugging output correctly identifies that put path.
intent_record.what: A new enum-to-string trace mapping entry was added: EM(rxrpc_call_put_recvmsg_peek_nowait, "PUT peek-nwt") inserted alongside the existing rxrpc_call_put_* mappings.
intent_record.how: This extends the tracing/debug output so that when the rxrpc_call_put_recvmsg_peek_nowait reason is used at runtime, it will be emitted with a defined human-readable label instead of being absent from the mapping.

intent_record.intent_summary: Add trace/debug event labels for recvmsg requeue-related RxRPC call states to improve runtime observability.
intent_record.what: Three new EM() trace/event mapping entries were added to the existing list: rxrpc_call_see_recvmsg_requeue mapped to "SEE recv-rqu", rxrpc_call_see_recvmsg_requeue_first mapped to "SEE recv-rqF", and rxrpc_call_see_recvmsg_requeue_move mapped to "SEE recv-rqM".
intent_record.how: This extends the set of named trace or debug event labels available at runtime so code can distinguish and report three recvmsg requeue-related states or actions that previously had no corresponding mapping, improving observability rather than changing core execution logic.

intent_record.intent_summary: Avoid notifying the socket on MSG_PEEK recvmsg calls so notifications only occur when queued data may actually be consumed.
intent_record.what: The condition before calling rxrpc_notify_socket(call) was changed from checking only whether call->recvmsg_queue is non-empty to additionally requiring that the MSG_PEEK flag is not set, by wrapping the queue check in !(flags & MSG_PEEK).
intent_record.how: At runtime, socket notification is now triggered only for normal receive operations that may consume queued data, and not for peek reads. This prevents a MSG_PEEK recvmsg call from causing the socket to be notified as if data had been consumed when the receive queue still contains data.

intent_record.intent_summary: Fix recvmsg call requeueing to safely handle already-queued calls, preserve correct queue order, and maintain proper call reference accounting.
intent_record.what: The requeue logic in rxrpc_recvmsg() was changed from always doing list_add(&call->recvmsg_link, &rx->recvmsg_q) under recvmsg_lock to conditionally handling three cases: add the call only if call->recvmsg_link is not on a list, do nothing to the list if the call is already the first entry, or move it to the queue head with list_move() if it is already linked but not first. The change also adds rxrpc_see_call() on newly added entries, adds rxrpc_put_call() calls for the already-first and moved cases, and renames the MSG_PEEK path's put-call trace reason from rxrpc_call_put_recvmsg to rxrpc_call_put_recvmsg_peek_nowait.
intent_record.how: At runtime, this prevents blindly re-adding a call that may already be linked on the recvmsg queue, avoiding duplicate or invalid list insertion and keeping queue ordering consistent by moving existing entries to the front only when needed. It also adjusts call reference/accounting so newly queued calls are recorded with a 'see' reference and existing queued calls have an extra reference dropped appropriately, while the MSG_PEEK path now uses a more specific accounting reason label.

relevance_review.reason: This change only adds a trace reason mapping for debugging output. It does not modify the recvmsg queue logic, list re-adding behavior, or checks around whether recvmsg_link is already queued, which are the core elements of the vulnerability.

The change only adds trace/debug event labels for observability. It does not modify the recvmsg queue logic, requeue conditions, list handling, or reference management that caused the list corruption vulnerability.

The root cause is incorrect re-queuing on the MSG_DONTWAIT error path causing recvmsg_q list corruption, while this group changes notification behavior for MSG_PEEK so sockets are not notified when data is only peeked. That does not address duplicate queue insertion or recvmsg_link state checks.

The group directly fixes the recvmsg requeue path by checking/safely handling already-queued calls and preserving reference accounting, which matches the root cause of blindly re-adding an already queued call and causing list corruption/mismatched references.

candidates.rationale: This line blindly re-added call->recvmsg_link to rx->recvmsg_q on the error requeue path without checking whether the link was already queued, directly causing list corruption.
This condition gates the erroneous requeue path for non-MSG_PEEK recvmsg handling, leading to the unsafe list_add and mismatched reference handling on the MSG_DONTWAIT error path.

bic_trace_step.reason: The diff is sufficient because it shows the exact recvmsg requeue error path in question. In this commit, a new `error_requeue_call:` path was added, and it unconditionally does `list_add(&call->recvmsg_link, &rx->recvmsg_q);` under `if (!(flags & MSG_PEEK))` after failing to get `call->user_mutex` or being interrupted while waiting for it. There is no check such as `list_empty()`/queued-state validation before re-adding `call->recvmsg_link` to `rx->recvmsg_q`. The root cause states that `rxrpc_recvmsg()` 'blindly re-added a call to rx->recvmsg_q on the MSG_DONTWAIT error path without checking whether call->recvmsg_link was already queued,' causing list corruption. That vulnerable construct is present here: `if (!mutex_trylock(&call->user_mutex)) { ret = -EWOULDBLOCK; if (flags & MSG_DONTWAIT) goto error_requeue_call; ... }` followed by `list_add(&call->recvmsg_link, &rx->recvmsg_q);`. Since the requeue is unconditional on that path and no duplicate-queue protection is shown, the bug is present. The fix is not present because there is still no guard preventing re-adding an already queued `recvmsg_link`.
